tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Booked date ranges and open windows for the three homes, from the live calendars (refreshed every 30 minutes). Ranges are start to end with end exclusive: a checkout day is open for a new check in. openWindows lists every gap at least as long as that home's minimum stay inside the window you ask for

tools.name: request_booking
tools.description: Sends a booking request to the owner on the guest's behalf, priced by the same engine as get_quote. This is request to book: the owner confirms by email to the guest with a payment link, and nothing is charged now. findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "get_quote" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: property, checkin, checkout, guests, dog, code

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "request_booking" stacks urgency/override words (never, mandatory, warning). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: Sends a booking request to the owner on the guest's behalf, priced by the same engine as get_quote. This is request to book: the owner confirms by email to the …

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_quote · Public sink: request_booking.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_quote · Public sink: request_booking

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "check_availability" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
